description: Cacik is a refreshing Turkish yogurt and cucumber dip, perfect for hot summer days or as a side to grilled meats. Made with cool yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, and fresh herbs, it offers a delightful balance of creamy, tangy, and savory flavors. This beloved appetizer is a staple in Turkish cuisine, known for its simplicity and vibrant taste.

ingredients.notes: Turkish süzme yoğurt or full-fat Greek yogurt
peeled and grated or finely diced

instructions.title: Prepare Cucumbers and Garlic
instructions.text: Peel and grate the cucumbers. If using very watery cucumbers, gently squeeze out any excess liquid using a clean kitchen towel. Finely mince the garlic cloves.

instructions.title: Combine Yogurt and Herbs
instructions.text: In a medium mixing bowl, place the thick plain yogurt. Add the finely chopped fresh mint and fresh dill (if using).

instructions.title: Mix Main Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared grated cucumbers and minced garlic to the yogurt and herb mixture. Stir well to combine all ingredients evenly.

instructions.title: Season and Adjust Consistency
instructions.text: Season the mixture with salt to taste. Gradually add cold water, one tablespoon at a time, stirring after each addition, until you achieve your desired consistency. Some prefer it thick, while others like it a bit thinner.

instructions.title: Chill for Flavor Development
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the cacik for at least 35 minutes. This chilling period allows the flavors to meld beautifully and ensures the dip is refreshingly cold when served.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Before serving, give the cacik a final stir. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and garnish with a few fresh mint leaves or a sprinkle of dried mint. Serve cold with crusty bread, grilled meats, or as part of a meze platter.

tips: For the most authentic taste, use a very thick, strained plain yogurt, like Turkish süzme yoğurt or a good quality full-fat Greek yogurt. Avoid low-fat or flavored yogurts.
If your cucumbers are very watery, grating them and then squeezing out excess moisture with a clean kitchen towel will prevent your cacik from becoming too thin.
Cacik is best served well-chilled. Prepare it at least 30 minutes in advance and refrigerate to allow the flavors to meld beautifully. You can make it a few hours ahead for best results.
